turns.prompt_text: I'm at the gas pump and I see there's 88, 87, and 91. What's the difference between all of these? I always just go with 87, which is super unleaded here at HyV.
turns.response_html:
Octane rating. These numbers represent how much the fuel can be compressed before it ignites; higher numbers resist "knocking" better in high-performance engines.

  • 87 (Regular): The standard for most everyday vehicles, including your Chevy Malibu.
  • 88 (E15): Contains 15% ethanol, which is cheaper but slightly less energy-dense than standard gasoline.
  • 91+ (Premium): Designed for high-compression or turbocharged engines that require extra stability to prevent premature combustion.

Stick with 87 for your Malibu unless the manual explicitly requires "Premium" fuel. Using a higher octane than your engine needs won't improve performance or fuel economy.
